stem: A data set consists of 6 positive integers. Its only mode is \(4\), its median is \(5\) and its mean is \(6\). What is the greatest possible value in the data set?
solution: The sum of the 6 integers is \(6 \cdot 6 = 36\). In order, call them \(a \le b \le c \le d \le e \le f\); the median gives \(c + d = 10\).
4 must appear at least twice, so it must be among \(a, b, c\), which forces \(c = 4\) and \(d = 6\), with \(b = 4\).
To make \(f\) as large as possible, make the others small: \(a = 1\). If \(e = 6\), then 6 would appear as often as 4, so \(e = 7\).
